key_facts: Patient is a man in his 60s
History of primary hyperparathyroidism 6 years prior to presentation
Patient refused therapeutic management for primary hyperparathyroidism
Elevated serum parathyroid hormone at 380 pmol/L
Large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger
Radiography showed complete lysis of the underlying phalanx and periosteal bone resorption
Chest radiograph revealed important deformation of the ribs
Thoracic CT scan revealed multiple lesions associated with multiple rib and vertebral fractures
Skull radiography showed pattern of trabecular resorption with 'salt-and-pepper' appearance

raw.rationale: The patient's history of primary hyperparathyroidism, elevated serum parathyroid hormone, hypercalcemia, and hypophosphatemia, combined with the presence of a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger and radiographic findings of bone resorption, are consistent with the diagnosis of Brown Tumor of Hyperparathyroidism. The histopathology of the finger tumor showing fibrous tissue, woven bone, and giant cells with multiple osteoclast-like nuclei further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Parathyroid Carcinoma
rejected.why: While parathyroid carcinoma can cause hyperparathyroidism, the presence of a single large tumor on the finger and the specific radiographic and histopathologic findings are more consistent with Brown Tumor of Hyperparathyroidism.

rejected.label: Primary Hyperparathyroidism
rejected.why: Primary hyperparathyroidism is a broader diagnosis that encompasses the patient's condition, but it does not specifically explain the presence of the large tumor on the finger.

rejected.label: Parathyroid Adenoma
rejected.why: Parathyroid adenoma is a possible cause of primary hyperparathyroidism, but it does not directly explain the bone lesions and tumor on the finger.

rejected.label: Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica
rejected.why: Osteitis fibrosa cystica is a condition characterized by bone resorption and cyst formation, but it is not a specific diagnosis that explains the patient's entire clinical presentation.

rejected.label: Hyperparathyroidism-Jaw Tumor Syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome is characterized by hyperparathyroidism, jaw tumors, and other features, but the patient's presentation does not specifically match this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Familial Isolated Hyperparathyroidism
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by familial primary hyperparathyroidism without other syndromic features, but it does not explain the patient's bone lesions and tumor on the finger.

rejected.label: Familial Hypocalciuric Hypercalcemia
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by hypercalcemia with low urinary calcium excretion, but the patient's presentation does not match this diagnosis.
